title: Accessibility of a small right lifting class
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$, with small Hom sets and small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] relative to $\mathcal U$. A category is locally presentable if it is cocomplete and, for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$, generated under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects whose Hom functors preserve those colimits. Here $\kappa$-filtered means every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms has a cocone, and regular means a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of size less than $\kappa$ still has size less than $\kappa$. A replete full subcategory $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal D$ is accessible as a subcategory if, for some infinite regular $\lambda\in\mathcal U$, it is closed under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits in $\mathcal D$ and generated under these colimits by a small set of its objects; replete means closed under isomorphism in $\mathcal D$. Let $\mathcal C$ be locally presentable and let $I$ be a small set of its morphisms. Use diagonal lifting as in [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]: $p:X\to Y$ belongs to $I^{\square}$ if for every $i:A\to B$ in $I$ and maps $u:A\to X$, $v:B\to Y$ with $pu=vi$, there is $h:B\to X$ with $hi=u$ and $ph=v$. Then the full subcategory of the arrow category $\mathcal C^{[1]}$ on $I^{\square}$ is replete and accessible as a subcategory. Objects of $\mathcal C^{[1]}$ are arrows and morphisms are commuting squares; its colimits are computed on source and target. No uniqueness of fillers, model-category structure, or restriction on the size of the endpoints of individual arrows is assumed.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\mathcal C^{[1]}$ and $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Fun}(I_{\rm disc}\times[1],\mathsf{Set}_{\mathcal U})$, where $I_{\rm disc}$ has objects the generating maps and only identity arrows, and $[1]$ has objects 0,1 and one nonidentity arrow $0\to1$. Both are locally presentable. To check the pullback hypothesis needed for $\mathcal A$, apply [lem-coef-accessible-monad-presentability] to a singleton family with value $\mathcal C$ and the identity monad. Its algebra equation $a1=1$ forces $a=1$, and every underlying map is an algebra map; thus its complete algebra category is exactly $\mathcal C$. In particular $\mathcal C$ has pullbacks. Apply [lem-coef-presheaf-local-presentability] with index $[1]^{\rm op}$ and values in $\mathcal C$ to obtain local presentability of $\mathcal A$. For $\mathcal D$, the same node supplies local presentability of small sets, whose pullbacks are the sets of pairs with equal images; apply its presheaf clause with index $(I_{\rm disc}\times[1])^{\rm op}$. All indexing categories here are $\mathcal U$-small.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 proof, printed p. 821: Hom-square functor and surjection test; details expanded by the worker.

proof.text: Colimits in either displayed diagram category are pointwise. Indeed, for a diagram of diagrams choose the colimit at each vertex. For each indexing arrow the compatible maps from its source diagram to the colimit at its target induce a unique map out of the source colimit, by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The identity and composition equations hold after precomposing with all structure maps and hence hold by uniqueness. A cocone into any other diagram then gives unique vertex maps; the same uniqueness verifies their naturality. This is the colimit universal property. Hom sets in $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal D$ are small: natural transformations are subsets of products of small Hom sets indexed by a small set.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 proof, printed p. 821: Hom-square functor and surjection test; details expanded by the worker.

proof.text: Write each $i\in I$ as $i:A_i\to B_i$. Apply [lem-coef-object-presentability-rank] to both $A_i$ and $B_i$, obtaining infinite regular cardinals $\tau_{i,0}$ and $\tau_{i,1}$ for their Hom functors. For each such cardinal take its set of smaller ordinals, and apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to this small family of small sets. Its bound is an infinite regular $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ strictly larger than every $\tau_{i,e}$. A $\kappa$-filtered category is $\tau_{i,e}$-filtered by the definition, since any diagram with fewer than $\tau_{i,e}$ morphisms has fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms. Hence both endpoint Hom functors preserve all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. For $I=\varnothing$ use the same bound lemma on the empty family.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 proof, printed p. 821: Hom-square functor and surjection test; details expanded by the worker.

proof.text: For $p:X\to Y$ define the small set $Q_i(p)=\{(u,v)\in\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,X)\times\operatorname{Hom}(B_i,Y):pu=vi\}$ and the function $H_i(p):\operatorname{Hom}(B_i,X)\to Q_i(p)$ by $h\mapsto(hi,ph)$. For a commuting square $(a,b):p\to p'$ with $p'a=bp$, send $h$ to $ah$ and $(u,v)$ to $(au,bv)$. The latter pair belongs to $Q_i(p')$, since $p'au=bpu=bvi$; the two functions form a commuting square because $(ahi,p'ah)=(ahi,bph)$. Identity and composition laws are componentwise function identities. These formulas therefore define a functor $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal D$, with $i$-component $H_i$.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 proof, printed p. 821: Hom-square functor and surjection test; details expanded by the worker.

proof.text: Let $J$ be any small $\kappa$-filtered category and $p_j:X_j\to Y_j$ a $J$-diagram with pointwise colimit $p:X\to Y$. There is a canonical description $Q_i(p_j)=\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,X_j)\times_{\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,Y_j)}\operatorname{Hom}(B_i,Y_j)$, using composition with $p_j$ and precomposition with $i$. By step 3 each of these three Hom diagrams has colimit its Hom set at $X$ or $Y$. Since $\kappa$ is infinite, $J$ is filtered. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] to this finite span of sets, obtaining the canonical bijection $\operatorname{colim}_j Q_i(p_j)\cong Q_i(p)$. The source comparison $\operatorname{colim}_j\operatorname{Hom}(B_i,X_j)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B_i,X)$ is also a bijection. These comparisons form a square of functions, since on a representative $h$ both routes give $(hi,ph)$ after applying the colimit maps. Thus each $H_i$ preserves these colimits, and pointwise computation in step 2 shows that $H$ preserves them. Only a finite limit of sets is interchanged with the colimit, even when $I$ is infinite.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 proof, printed p. 821: Hom-square functor and surjection test; details expanded by the worker.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal D$ be the full subcategory of families of surjections $s_i:S_i\to T_i$. It is replete: conjugating a surjection by two bijections is a surjection. It is closed under every small filtered colimit in $\mathcal D$. Indeed, fix $i$ and $t\in\operatorname{colim}_jT_{j,i}$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] gives a representative $t_j\in T_{j,i}$. Surjectivity at that stage supplies $x_j\in S_{j,i}$ with $s_{j,i}(x_j)=t_j$, and its colimit image maps to $t$. Step 2 computes this as the required component of the ambient colimit.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 proof, p. 821, surjective maps form an accessible subcategory; filtered-colimit closure expanded, using Stacks Tags 04AX and 002V.

proof.text: Fix a family $s=(s_i:S_i\twoheadrightarrow T_i)\in\mathcal V$. Let $P$ be the poset of finite subsets $E$ of the small disjoint union $\coprod_i S_i$, ordered by inclusion. It is small, nonempty (it contains $\varnothing$), and filtered because $E\cup E'$ bounds $E,E'$. Put $E_i=\{x:(i,x)\in E\}$ and define $s^E_i:E_i\to s_i(E_i)$ by restriction of $s_i$. These are surjections with finite endpoints, and all but finitely many components are $\varnothing\to\varnothing$. Inclusion of finite subsets gives commuting squares, so the $s^E$ form a $P$-diagram in $\mathcal V$ with a cocone to $s$. At each source component its union is $S_i$, since every $x$ lies in a singleton finite subset; at each target component its union is $T_i$, since each $t$ has some preimage $x$ and hence lies in $s_i(E_i)$ for such a singleton. For a compatible family of functions out of the source subsets, define its value at $x$ using any $E$ containing $(i,x)$; two choices agree after inclusion into their union. For the target subsets, define its value at $t$ using any $E$ with $t\in s_i(E_i)$, which exists by surjectivity; two choices again agree in their union. These definitions give the unique functions on $S_i$ and $T_i$ extending the cocone. Their square commutes because it commutes on every $E_i$. Therefore these unions are colimits of sets by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and step 2 identifies $s=\operatorname{colim}_{E\in P}s^E$ in $\mathcal D$.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 proof, p. 821: explicit finite-subset generation argument for the surjection test, simultaneously for the small generating set I.

proof.text: There is a small fixed family of objects containing an isomorphic copy of every $s^E$ used in step 7. Namely choose a finite subset $F\subseteq I$, natural numbers $n_i,m_i$ for $i\in F$, and surjective functions $\{0,\ldots,n_i-1\}\to\{0,\ldots,m_i-1\}$; use the empty arrow at all other indices. Finite subsets of a small set, finite lists of natural numbers, and functions between finite sets each range over small sets, so these data form a small set $G\subseteq\mathcal V$. Each $s^E$ is isomorphic to a member of $G$ by numbering its finitely many source and target elements. For the small diagram in step 7 choose such an isomorphism $\theta_E:g_E\xrightarrow{\sim}s^E$ at each object, and replace a transition $k_{EE'}$ by $\theta_{E'}^{-1}k_{EE'}\theta_E$. Cancellation verifies the diagram laws and yields an isomorphism of diagrams, so the same colimit is a filtered colimit of objects from $G$. Steps 6-8 prove exactly that $\mathcal V$ is an accessible subcategory, with witnessing cardinal $\aleph_0$. This also covers $I=\varnothing$: there is one empty family and its constant one-object presentation.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 proof, p. 821: smallness of the finite-surjection generators, with the simultaneous family argument made explicit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-accessible-full-inverse-image] to $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal V$. Step 1 proves local presentability of both ambient categories, step 2 checks Hom-smallness and ambient colimits, step 5 proves preservation of small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by $H$, and steps 6-8 check repleteness and accessibility of $\mathcal V$ in precisely the ambient-colimit sense of that node. Its conclusion is that the full inverse image $H^{-1}\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal A$ is replete and accessible. No common cardinal for the input and conclusion is required.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.7, p. 820, applied once to the family-valued functor; realizes the small intersection in Corollary A.2.6.8 without an additional intersection theorem.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], membership of $p$ in $I^{\square}$ means that for each $i:A_i\to B_i$ and each $(u,v)\in Q_i(p)$ there exists $h:B_i\to X$ with $(hi,ph)=(u,v)$. This is exactly surjectivity of every function $H_i(p)$, and hence exactly $H(p)\in\mathcal V$. Thus the full subcategory on $I^{\square}$ equals $H^{-1}\mathcal V$ on objects and on all commuting squares. Step 9 gives the claimed repleteness and accessibility. The test asserts existence of $h$, never uniqueness, and the only bounds chosen in step 3 concern the fixed small family of generating endpoints, not the endpoints $X,Y$ of $p$.
